title: Bill Belichick and North Carolina speak out amid buyout rumors and poor play - NewsBreak
text:
By Matthew Neschis ,
33 minutes ago Bill Belichick has doubled down on his dedication to North Carolina amid swirling speculation that the Tar Heels head coach has already explored potential escape routes.
Belichick's stint in Chapel Hill has been an unmitigated catastrophe so far, with controversies and messy performances becoming daily occurrences .
In the most recent off-field nightmare for the NFL icon, cornerbacks coach Armond Hawkins received a suspension for violating NCAA rules .
READ MORE: Tommy Fleetwood's opinion on Bryson DeChambeau clash after new Ryder Cup footage emerges
READ MORE: Travis Kelce could have another fine coming after Chiefs loss to Jaguars
The Tar Heels haven't helped calm the storm with their on-field displays, as North Carolina sits at a dismal 2-3 record after being outscored 120-33 by Power Four rivals.
Despite the turbulent beginning to Belichick's North Carolina chapter, both parties declared their willingness to continue this venture.
"I'm fully committed to UNC Football and the program we're building here," Belichick said in an official statement posted to X on Wednesday.
North Carolina athletics director Bubba Cunningham reciprocated the sentiment, stating: "Coach Belichick has the full support of the Department of Athletics and University."
While Belichick and Cunningham publicly expressed their commitment to remain united, recent whispers suggest otherwise.
Per 247 Sports , North Carolina engaged in "preliminary conversations" about dismissing Belichick - an expensive move that would require the university to honor the $20 million buyout specified in his contract. It seems Belichick is seriously considering his options, with journalist Ollie Connolly revealing he has "discussed buyout options with North Carolina's hierarchy."
During these talks, Belichick has "signaled a willingness to trigger his own $1 million buyout if he can find a soft landing with another team or in media."
To prepare for Belichick's possible exit, his coaching staff members have reportedly reached out to other programs likely heading to the College Football Playoff, hoping to secure positions during the postseason.
In North Carolina's most recent outing — a crushing 38-10 defeat to Clemson — Belichick's team trailed 28-3 after just one quarter before heading into the locker room down by 32 points.
Throughout the past fortnight, UNC coaching staff members told Connolly that Belichick has appeared "weird" and "distant" when interacting with his colleagues.
During the Tar Heels' bye week, multiple coaches admitted they struggled to reach him by phone.
